## Overview

`add("2", "3")` returns the string `"23"`, not the number `5`. `calc.js` has one exported function and no numeric conversion, so two numeric strings concatenate instead of summing.

## How It Works

The whole file is 46 bytes and one line decides the behavior.

```js
export function add(a, b) {
  return a + b;
}
```

Line 2, `return a + b;`, hands both arguments straight to the JavaScript `+` operator. `+` is overloaded. If either operand is a string, it coerces the other operand to a string and concatenates. Numeric addition happens only when neither operand is a string.

So `"2" + "3"` gives `"23"` by the language rule, and the numeric values never matter. The function applies no `Number()`, no `parseInt()`, and no validation.

## Measured Results

Command run in `/private/var/folders/11/m_kwnqr97632l_cjt0mhytvh0000gn/T/pstack-two-live-GQdOxN/work` (measured, Node v24.21.0).

```
node --input-type=module -e 'import {add} from "./calc.js"; const r = add("2","3"); console.log(JSON.stringify(r), typeof r); console.log(JSON.stringify(add(2,3)), typeof add(2,3)); console.log(JSON.stringify(add("2",3)), typeof add("2",3));'
```

Raw output.

```
"23" string
5 number
"23" string
```

A read-only subagent independently read the source and reached the same three results from the ECMAScript `+` rule. That part is inferred from the spec, since the read-only mode it ran in strips shell access and it could not execute `node`. The numbers above are what I measured directly.

## Where Things Live

`calc.js` is the only file in the working tree, and the sole commit touching it is `4aa8fb3 calc`. There is no caller, no test, and no type annotation in the repo, so nothing else depends on `add` today.

## Gotchas

The name says arithmetic and the body says concatenation whenever a string arrives, and the caller gets no error. `add(undefined, 1)`, `add(null, 1)`, and `add([], 1)` behave the same way, since `+` also coerces those to strings. If a caller needs the sum, it must convert first, for example with `add(Number(a), Number(b))`, and the function itself cannot tell the difference.
